findings.claim: The change reaches the MCP server's tool output, which is not in the touch-point list: both `get_collection` and `add_to_collection` now return an extra `on_home` field, and the spec's §7 mentions only `get_collection`.
findings.impact: An MCP client (an LLM agent) sees a new `on_home` field in two tool outputs. The spec accepts this for `get_collection` but never mentions `add_to_collection`, and neither tool's tests pin the shape. Nothing breaks for a user today; the reach is simply unplanned.
findings.evidence: backend/app/routers/collections.py:76 adds `on_home` to `_to_detail`, which also builds the add-items (collections.py:242) and reorder (collections.py:303) responses. mcp-server/src/tools/collections.ts:67-79 spreads `...rest` of the detail into its output, so `on_home` passes through. mcp-server/src/tools/write.ts:269-275 returns the raw `POST .../collections/{id}/items` response, which now carries `on_home`. Neither `mcp-server/` nor these tools appears under the spec's `## Touch points`.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read-only). Calling the MCP `add_to_collection` tool against this build returns a JSON body that includes `on_home`.

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariant covers MCP output, and the extra field is harmless. It is still an unplanned reach that the touch-point list (and, for add_to_collection, spec §7) leaves out.

findings.proposed_fix: Add `mcp-server/src/tools/collections.ts` (get_collection) and `mcp-server/src/tools/write.ts` (add_to_collection) to the touch points as read-only pass-throughs, through a revision in invariants.md.

specification_compliance: Every file the diff changes maps to a listed touch point, apart from the implicit spec, INDEX and review files. The backend models, database, schemas, home_shortcuts router, main, collections, drives and backend tests are listed. On the frontend, api.ts, types, HomeAppEntries, DriveHome, FolderToolbar, usePinnedFolders, FolderBrowser, CollectionDetail, SmartFolderSaveButton, useSmartFolders, the messages files and the e2e-components fixture and cases are listed. So are docs/reference/api.md and docs/user-guide/file-browsing.md.

DESIGN.md is edited, not only read. The touch points list it under 'Rules passed through', and docs/process/spec-and-design.md:41-43 counts 'rules and conventions it passes through' as a touch point, so I do not report it as unplanned.

Several existing vitest files that mock `@/lib/api` gained `getHomeShortcuts`: DriveHome.test, accent-budget, driveHomeFailureState, driveHomeSectionOrder, driveHomeTreeClosable, uploadZoneHosts, DriveHome.driveChange and DriveHome.icons. CollectionDetail.test had an assertion changed. The specific bullet names only the files that mock usePinnedFolders, but the generic 'Frontend tests (vitest)' entry covers these.

Some listed touch points are not changed by the diff: smart_folders.py gets `on_home` through `from_attributes` and the model property, and usePinnedFolders.test.ts, FolderContent and FolderTreePane are unchanged. That is a list wider than needed, not an unplanned reach.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The MCP `add_to_collection` output gains `on_home`; spec §7 discusses only `get_collection` and `list_collections`.
regression_risks: HomeAppEntries' TILE / TILE_LABEL change (max-w-16rem and a wrapped label span with line-clamp/truncate) applies to every builtin and addon tile, not only shortcuts; the SPEC-CORE-073 e2e cases are the guard.

PinnedFolderResponse and CollectionDetailResponse now require `on_home`. The only constructors I found (drives.py:1598,1623 and collections.py:61) pass it, but any future constructor that leaves it out fails validation.
test_coverage: The MCP server's tests use mocked API responses, so they do not exercise the new `on_home` pass-through.
The sidebar consumers of pins and smart-folders (useSidebarData, SidebarSmartFoldersSection, Sidebar.tsx) are unchanged and have no test asserting that they ignore `on_home`; the spec says they do.
